newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles County prepares $1.3 bln note deal.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles County prepares $1.3 bln note deal.

text.p: Los Angeles County plans to come to market on Wednesday with $1.3 billion of tax and revenue anticipation notes in its first unenhanced short-term note deal in two seasons.
For the last two years, the county has been forced to buy letters of credit because of concerns on Wall Street about the its fiscal condition.
But last week, Moody's Investors Service Inc rated the county's short-term notes MIG-1, Standard & Poor's Corp rated them SP-1-plus, and Fitch Investors Service Inc assigned them an F-1-plus grade.

The ratings -- the highest offered -- will allow the county to issue its tax and revenue anticipation notes on Wednesday without a letter of credit, saving the county an estimated $2 million, county finance officials said.
"I don't expect it (the note sale) to be a blow out," said Maureen Sicotte, the county's director of public finance. "But I hope that there's good market reception."
